subject: Novacorp: portal login failing behind corporate jump-host (webauthn origin mismatch)
messages:
From: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@novacorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Novacorp Procurement <procure@novacorp.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Unable to accept supplier invite — login blocked behind corporate jump-host

Hi Mina,

We've been trying to onboard our supplier users into your Coupa/Ariba portal (purchase flows for our renewed contract) but several of our users see an error when they click the invite link: “Authentication failed — unexpected origin.” The affected users sit behind our corporate jump-host / proxy fabric and are using hardware security keys (FIDO2) for MFA.

I attached a screenshot and the edge logs from a failed login. We can reproduce this consistently from our jump-host environment but not from home networks. Can your team advise? We need PO issuance this week and this is blocking the AP process.

Attachments: novacorp_screenshot.png, webauthn_logs.txt

Thanks,
Miguel
Miguel Torres
Head of Procurement
Novacorp

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unable to accept supplier invite — login blocked behind corporate jump-host

Hi Miguel — sorry you're hitting this. Thanks for the logs and screenshot (received).

Looping in Marissa from Onboarding and Karthik from Platform Security so we can triage. A few quick questions while they join:
- Can you confirm which portal (Coupa / Ariba / Workday / Zip) the invite was for? Your logs mention Ariba but the invite link looks like a Coupa vanity URL.
- Are your users hitting this from a shared gateway IP (jump-host) or from an internal proxy that rewrites origins?
- Rough ETA for when you need PO cut? You mentioned this week; what's the hard deadline?

We'll take a look and propose either a short-term bypass (email-only confirmation or service account) and a longer-term origin allowlist fix if needed.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@novacorp.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unable to accept supplier invite — login blocked behind corporate jump-host

Hi Miguel — thanks for sending the logs.

Preliminary read: the WebAuthn assertion is failing server-side due to an origin mismatch. Our authentication stack validates the relying party origin in the attestation; if your jump-host rewrites navigation or injects a different Host/Origin header, the browser will reject the assertion and the server will mark it as "unexpected origin."

Two immediate options to unblock PO flow:
1) Issue a time-limited service account for Novacorp supplier users so procurement can complete onboarding (we can automate PO reconciliation after).
2) Send invite links that perform email-confirm only (skip hardware key step) — less ideal for your security posture but works as a stopgap.

To proceed with (1) we need: saml_metadata_novacorp.xml (if you're using SAML SSO) or a list of allowed jump-host origins we can add to the tenant allowlist. If you'd like (2) we can also provide a one-time invite flow.

Attaching our SAML metadata sample and a short checklist for service account creation.

Attachments: saml_metadata_novacorp.xml (sample)

—Marissa

From: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@novacorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unable to accept supplier invite — login blocked behind corporate jump-host

Thanks Marissa — this matches our internal engineer's read. Confirming: this is for the Ariba-hosted supplier portal vanity link (we have a mix of purchase flows). The jump-host does rewrite the Origin header in certain egress flows to route traffic through a managed gateway; our security team enforces FIDO2 everywhere so asking them to disable it temporarily is tough.

We can share the jump-host origin list but the list is large (different egress clusters per office). Would you be willing to support a tenant-level alias/origin that maps the invite domain through our gateway, or alternatively issue a temporary service account for the procurement team so they can finish onboarding and PO submission? We really need PO confirmation by EOD Monday (16 Nov) for the vendor to be paid on this cycle.

I can also loop in Ariba Support if you want — they suggested the origin must match the relying party ID exactly for WebAuthn.

—Miguel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@novacorp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unable to accept supplier invite — login blocked behind corporate jump-host

Hi Miguel — quick technical note from Platform Security:

You're correct that WebAuthn relies on exact origin/relyingPartyId match. If the gateway rewrites the origin, authentication will fail. We have three practical paths:
A) Add Novacorp jump-host origins to the tenant allowlist (requires a list of canonical origins; we can add wildcard subnets only in very limited cases).
B) Create a temporary service account scoped to the procurement mailbox that can accept invites on behalf of users and complete PO submission — we can restrict it to a single-day window.
C) Arrange a short troubleshooting session with Ariba Support to update the relyingPartyId mapping for your tenant (preferred long-term fix).

For (B) we will provision the account and provide a README and an expiring API key; for (A) we need the most-used egress origins (a short list of 4–6 is usually sufficient).

I'll open an internal support ticket and assign SOC approval to add origins if we go that route. If you authorize (B), reply with the procurement user list and preferred expiry time.

References: https://docs.redwood.ai/platform/webauthn-compat

—Karthik
Platform Security, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unable to accept supplier invite — login blocked behind corporate jump-host

Miguel — thanks for the quick responses and for confirming the timeline.

Next steps agreed:
- We're provisioning a temporary procurement service account (scope: accept invites + submit PO) that will expire 2026-11-17 23:59 PST. See attached temp_service_account_readme.md for credentials and usage.
- If you can send the top 4 egress origins (even if approximate), we'll open the allowlist escalation with SOC in parallel so your users don't hit the issue on future invites.
- We're scheduling a 30-minute troubleshooting call with Ariba Support + our Platform Security at 14:00 PST on Tuesday 17 Nov to align on a permanent relyingPartyId mapping. I'll send a calendar invite shortly.

Attachments: temp_service_account_readme.md

I'll monitor the ticket (INC-20261112-9842) and confirm once the account is live. If PO still needs to be pushed through today, reply-all with the procurement user list and I'll provision the account immediately.

Best,
Mina
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
